q: What is hp-psm-v2 in the hardship-programs project?
a: hp-psm-v2 is propensity matching with a 0.05 caliper, 4:1 on six covariates plus transaction drop and bureau delta. It supersedes hp-psm-v1 and gives a 30-to-60 roll effect of -4.7pp on hardship-programs-holdout-2025q4 (n=6,310 enrolled).

q: What came of exp-405 in the hardship-programs project?
a: Six-month plans cut the 30-to-60 roll by 5.2pp against 2.6pp for three-month plans. That led to find-hp-plan-length, and dec-hp-6mo-default made six months the default plan length.

q: What inputs does hp-rollmodel-v1 in the hardship-programs project use?
a: hp-rollmodel-v1 uses the monthly transition matrix in ds-hp-roll-matrix and takes its enrolment effect from hp-psm-v2 (-4.7pp on the 30-to-60 roll). Its scenario output is a -0.9pp change in long-run charge-off per enrolled account.

q: What is the current hardship-programs estimate of the 30-to-60 roll effect of enrolment that the team reports?
a: -4.7pp from hp-psm-v2 (exp-408), per find-hp-effect-v2. It replaces the -6.1pp adjusted estimate, with the -3.9pp DiD as robustness check.

q: What share of enrolled accounts are current 12 months after plan end against matched controls, and on how many enrolled accounts?
a: 61% of enrolled accounts against 52% of matched controls, on ds-hp-cure-tracking with n=9,870 enrolled accounts that have a full 12-month window (exp-406).

q: Why did the hardship-programs reported effect move from -6.1pp to -4.7pp?
a: hp-psm-v2 added a 0.05 caliper and the transaction-drop and bureau-delta covariates, and the max standardised mean difference after matching fell to 0.08. find-hp-effect-v2 superseded find-hp-adjusted-effect on that basis.
